findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Twice-interrupted capture of reused mutable handing loses spend on checkpoint replacement
findings.smallest_reproduction: E/test_e.py::test_native_capture_pair[False]: seal live reader through _desk, dispatch once (settles spend), interrupt _items at initial capture and recovery using trace/profile checkpoints, replace ledger in the previously returned dict with saved pre-spend checkpoint, dispatch original action again. No source mutation.
findings.actual_result: First pin raises KeyboardInterrupt; later rollback is accepted and execution count reaches 2. Log: detached=False, refused=False, calls=2.
findings.expected_result: The handed spend remains an obligation; later rollback is refused and calls remains 1.
findings.trust_boundary: Execution owner legitimately hands canonical objects then replaces account on restore; interrupts are native control flow. No source/private account mutation. Crosses documented observation-forwardness contract; not a generic reservation or at-most-once requirement.
findings.proposed_correction: For this replacement family, owner-publish a detached dict pair whose membership is not subsequently mutated; preserve referenced spent account objects across replacement. Paired test_native_capture_pair[True] uses dict copies and refuses redispatch (calls=1), without acknowledgement. This is a bounded sufficient control, not a universal cure: nested account mutation and interruptions before any stable publication need separate lifecycle decisions. Additional reader-local retry alone has no demonstrated guarantee under repeated interruption.

changed_code_assessment: _retained_entry follows _read_once ordering: ledger BudgetCharge normalization then sorted JSON/default=str and owner readback; experiment scientific to_json then ScientificEvaluation readback then writability. No second serializer policy found. R17 controls and new ordering controls demonstrate numeric-key parity without silent rollback acceptance.
